_comment: The switches for how a slide gets its picture. Edit this file, commit, done.
The order below is the order they are tried, and the percentages are what
Wikimedia measured when they solved this same problem for unillustrated
Wikipedia articles (about 500 matches, six languages, expert reviewers):

subjectPicture._why: The picture attached to the story's own subject. 85-95% right in Wikimedia's test, the best method anyone has published. A picture of the pygmy hog, not of a nature reserve somewhere else.

librarysearch._why: Searching a picture library by words from the story. 20-40% right in the same test, and it is what produced the Texas nature centre for an Oregon wetland. OFF by Stefan's decision of 2026-09-27: a picture that is only thematically right is rejected, and the number graphic takes its place.

editorCheck._why: Our own editor looks at the chosen picture and may reject it. ON since Stefan's OK of 2026-09-27, after a test on 108 published stories found about one picture in four wrong without it. It needs an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret on the repository. With the flag on and no key, or any failure of the check, the picture is LEFT OUT and the slide shows its number, so a missing key costs pictures, never a Monday. Cost: one small picture question per named subject, at most five a week.

numberGraphic._why: Always last and never switched off. One figure the editor already published. Zero copyright surface, never the wrong picture, always available.
